title: Zardozi gold-wire embroidery
summary: Zardozi is the heavy metal-thread embroidery of northern India. Makers stretch velvet or silk on a wooden frame and stitch down coiled gold and silver wire, spangles and stones with a hooked needle, building raised shapes of mango, flower and leaf.
howToPlay: Pick a wire or stone from the reels and a shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the velvet to stitch it down; the mirror partner on the other half is stitched too.
Copy the plan beside the frame, then press Check.
rules: The panel mirrors left to right, so each shape you place is also stitched on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its metal or stone both match the plan.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; undo and clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Zardozi (from the Persian words for gold and embroidery) has been practised in northern Indian workshops for centuries and flourished in royal courts. Craftspeople still work in teams around a large frame, each with a hooked needle.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original arrangements in the style of the tradition)
